extracted.intended_audience: researchers, methodologists and practitioners selecting or developing resilience measurement scales (psychometricians, health researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic/methodological evaluation of resilience measurement scales' psychometric properties to inform selection, development and use in research, clinical and population settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the domain of interest is comprehensively sampled by the items in the questionnaire (the extent to which the measure represents all facets of the construct under question).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rating: A clear description of measurement aim, target population, concept(s) being measured, and the item selection AND target population and (investigators OR experts) were involved in item selection. Intermediate: clear description lacking OR only target population involved OR doubtful design/method. Negative: no target population involvement. No information: score 0. Emphasises involvement of the target group in item selection and pilot work; items should accurately reflect underlying concepts and theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which items in a (sub)scale are intercorrelated, thus measuring the same construct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rating: Factor analyses performed on adequate sample size (7 * #items AND >=100) AND Cronbach's alpha(s) calculated per dimension AND Cronbach's alpha(s) between 0.70 and 0.95. Intermediate: No factor analysis OR doubtful design/method. Negative: Cronbach's alpha(s) <0.70 or >0.95 despite adequate design/method. No information: score 0. (Guidance implies perform factor analysis, report alphas for subscales and whole scales; avoid alphas <0.70 or >0.95.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which scores on a particular questionnaire relate to a gold standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rating: Convincing arguments that the comparator is a true 'gold' standard AND correlation with gold standard >=0.70. Intermediate: No convincing argument that gold is 'gold' OR doubtful design/method. Negative: Correlation with gold <0.70 despite adequate design/method. No information: score 0. Notes the practical problem that no accepted gold standard for resilience typically exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which scores on a particular questionnaire relate to other measures in a manner consistent with theoretically derived hypotheses concerning the concepts being measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rating: Specific hypotheses were formulated AND at least 75% of the results are in accordance with these hypotheses. Intermediate: Doubtful design or method (e.g. no hypotheses). Negative: Less than 75% of hypotheses confirmed despite adequate design/methods. No information: score 0. Emphasises formulating and testing explicit hypotheses about expected associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (Agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the scores on repeated measures are close to each other (absolute measurement error).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rating: SDC < MIC OR MIC outside the LOA OR convincing arguments that agreement is acceptable. Intermediate: Doubtful design or method OR (MIC not defined AND no convincing arguments that agreement is acceptable). Negative: MIC <= SDC OR MIC equals or inside LOA despite adequate design/method. No information: score 0. (Defines SDC = smallest detectable difference; MIC = minimal important change; LOA = limits of agreement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (Reliability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which patients can be distinguished from each other despite measurement errors (relative measurement error).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rating: ICC or weighted Kappa >= 0.70. Intermediate: Doubtful design or method. Negative: ICC or weighted Kappa < 0.70 despite adequate design/method. No information: score 0. (Guidance: report test-retest statistics such as ICC/weighted Kappa to demonstrate stability.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability of a questionnaire to detect clinically important changes over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rating: SDC or SDC < MIC OR MIC outside LOA OR RR > 1.96 OR AUC >= 0.70. Intermediate: Doubtful design or method. Negative: SDC or SDC >= MIC OR MIC equals or inside LOA OR RR <= 1.96 or AUC < 0.70 despite adequate design/method. No information: score 0. (Practical note: responsiveness analyses are especially important when using a measure to evaluate change in response to an intervention; the review awarded responsiveness points to scales reporting change scores over time.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Floor and ceiling effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of respondents who achieved the lowest or highest possible score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rating: <= 15% of the respondents achieved the highest or lowest possible scores. Intermediate: Doubtful design or method. Negative: >15% of the respondents achieved highest or lowest possible scores despite adequate design/methods. No information: score 0. (Guidance: report proportion at extremes to ensure measure can discriminate across range.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which one can assign qualitative meaning to quantitative scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rating: Mean and SD scores presented of at least four relevant subgroups of patients AND MIC defined. Intermediate: Doubtful design or method OR less than four subgroups OR no MIC defined. No information: score 0. (Guidance: provide subgroup norms and define minimally important change to aid interpretation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate scoring of psychometric properties
rubrics_metrics.description: A numerical overall score to summarise psychometric quality across criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each property scored using symbols: + = 2 points; ? = 1 point; - = 0 points; 0 = 0 points. Total score range 0-18. This aggregate score is intended to give researchers/practitioners a clear overall indicator while the framework still reports individual property outcomes. (The review used this method to aid decision-making but also reported the separate quality assessment results.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and reporting of measurement error/change metrics (SDC, MIC, SEM, AUC, RR, LOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit use, definition and reporting of metrics that quantify measurement error and meaningful change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided: SDC = smallest detectable difference (smallest within-person change above measurement error); MIC = minimal important change (smallest difference perceived as beneficial by patients); SEM = standard error of measurement; AUC = area under the curve; RR = responsiveness ratio; LOA = limits of agreement. Guidance for positive ratings and thresholds are applied across reproducibility/responsiveness/interpretability criteria (e.g. SDC < MIC or MIC outside LOA; AUC >= 0.70; RR > 1.96). Authors should define MIC and report these statistics to demonstrate meaningful change beyond measurement error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target population involvement and piloting in item selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Involvement of intended respondents and experts in item generation and selection, and piloting to ensure acceptability and content relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive content validity requires involvement of target population and/or experts in item selection and pilot testing. Guidance emphasises that measures developed without target-group involvement (or without pilot work) may lack content validity and acceptability; initial piloting/consultation with qualitative feedback can identify likely respondent burden and improve uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical and conceptual grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the measure is conceptually/theoretically adequate and items reflect the underlying resilience construct and its multiple levels (individual, relational, community, culture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures should be theoretically grounded and explicitly define the resilience construct they intend to measure. The review flags that lack of theoretical clarity can undermine a measure's appropriateness (e.g. measures that treat resilience as fixed trait vs dynamic process). Extract and report evidence regarding theoretical basis as part of quality appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability/usability (acceptability, length, cultural relevance, mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical considerations affecting whether a questionnaire is appropriate for a given population and study purpose (length/time burden, mode of completion, cultural/contextual relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the aim of measurement and the target population: long questionnaires may increase non-response and missing data; cultural adaptation and meaningfulness are essential (e.g. CYRM developed across 11 countries may be preferable for cross-national surveys). Pilot for acceptability; ensure mode (self-report) and length suit respondents and setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of measure with study aim (purpose-driven selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a measure according to intended use (e.g. outcome evaluation/change detection vs cross-sectional association studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Ask 'what do you want to use it for?'. If evaluating change, prioritise responsiveness and test-retest reliability. For cross-sectional or multivariate analyses, prioritise good content and construct validity and internal consistency. Researchers should ascertain reliability (e.g. test-retest) prior to inclusion in evaluations aimed at detecting change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing/absent psychometric information
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat scales with incomplete or absent validation evidence within the quality framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no information regarding a relevant psychometric criterion is provided the lowest score (0) is awarded for that criterion. Reviewers should search for supporting papers that may supply missing psychometric data (e.g. subsequent applications reporting internal consistency or construct validity) and incorporate them where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting expectations for users of measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers using resilience measures should report relevant validation statistics when employing a scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper urges authors to report validation statistics (reliability, validity, responsiveness, interpretability metrics) when using measures so future reviews and users can judge appropriateness. This includes presenting mean/SD by subgroups, MIC, test-retest reliability, factor analyses, and floor/ceiling proportions.
